questions.question: In the circuit shown in figure X is an element which always absorbs power. During a particular operations, it sets up a current of \(1\text{ amp}\) in the direction shown and absorbs a power \(P_{\text{x}}\). It is possible that X can absorb the same power \(P_{\text{x}}\) for another current \(i\), the value of this current is
questions.explanation: Applying KVL, \[V_X=6-i\] Since element \(X\) always absorbs power, \[P_X=V_Xi \ \Rightarrow \ P_X=i(6-i)\] For the given operating condition, i=1A \[\Rightarrow P_X=1(6-1)=5~\text{W}\] Let another current \(i\) produce the same absorbed power. \[i(6-i)=5 \ \Rightarrow \ i^2-6i+5=0\] \[(i-1)(i-5)=0\] \[i=1~\text{A} \qquad \text{or} \qquad i=5~\text{A}\] Since the question asks for another current, \[i=5~\text{A}\] Therefore, \[\boxed{\textbf{C. }5~\text{A}}\]

questions.question: The \(v\text{-}i\) characteristic as seen from the terminal pair \((A, B)\) of the network of Fig. 1 is shown in the Fig. (2). If an inductance of value \(6\text{ mH}\) is connected across the terminal -- pair \((A, B)\), the time constant of the system will be
options: unknown, unless the actual network is specified
questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance of the network can be found out from slope of the given curve; \[R_{th} = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{8}{4\times10^{-3}} = 2000~\Omega\] \[R_{th}=2~\text{k}\Omega\] Hence, the network can be replaced by its Thevenin equivalent. When a \(6~\text{mH}\) inductor is connected across terminals \(A\) and \(B\), the time constant is \[\tau=\frac{L}{R_{th}}\] \[\tau = \frac{6\times10^{-3}}{2\times10^{3}}= 3\times10^{-6}\ \text{s}\] Hence, the correct answer is \[\boxed{\textbf{A. }3~\mu\text{s}}\]

questions.subject: network-theory
questions.question: A coil (which can be modeled as a series RL circuit) has been designed for high - Q performance at a rated voltage and a specified frequency. If the frequency of operation is doubled, and the coil is operated at the same rated voltage, then the Q-factor and the active power P consumed by the coil will be affected as follows
options: P is doubled, Q is halved
P is halved, Q is doubled
P remains constant, Q is doubled
P is decreased 4 times, Q is doubled
questions.explanation:
The Quality factor of a series RL circuit is defined as: \[Q = \frac{\omega L}{R}\] When the operating frequency is doubled, the new angular frequency becomes \(\omega_{1} = 2\omega\). The modified quality factor \(Q_{1}\) is given by: \[Q_{1} = \frac{\omega_{1} L}{R} = \frac{2\omega L}{R} = 2Q\] Hence, the quality factor \(Q\) is doubled. The active power \(P\) dissipated by the series circuit is given by: \[P = I^2 R\] The magnitude of the current \(I\) in a series RL circuit connected to a voltage source \(V\) is expressed as: \[I = \frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + (\omega L)^2}}\] Substituting the expression for current \(I\) into the active power formula: \[P = \left[\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + (\omega L)^2}}\right]^2 \times R = \frac{V^2 \cdot R}{R^2 + (\omega L)^2}\] Factoring out \(R^2\) from the denominator: \[P = \frac{V^2 \cdot R}{R^2 \left[1 + \left(\frac{\omega L}{R}\right)^2\right]} = \frac{V^2}{R \left[1 + \left(\frac{\omega L}{R}\right)^2\right]}\] Since \(Q = \frac{\omega L}{R}\), the equation simplifies to: \[P = \frac{V^2}{R(1 + Q^2)}\] Given that the coil has a high quality factor (\(Q^2 \gg 1\)), we can approximate \(1 + Q^2 \approx Q^2\): \[P \approx \frac{V^2}{R \cdot Q^2}\] When the frequency is doubled, the new active power \(P_{1}\) becomes: \[P_{1} = \frac{V^2}{R \cdot (Q_{1})^2}\] Substituting \(Q_{1} = 2Q\) into the relation: \[P_{1} = \frac{V^2}{R \cdot (2Q)^2} = \frac{V^2}{4R \cdot Q^2}\] \[P_{1} = \frac{P}{4}\] Therefore, the active power \(P\) decreases by 4 times. \[\boxed{(d)\textit{P is decreased 4 times, Q is doubled}}\]
Key points
  • For a high-\(Q\) coil (\(Q \gg 1\)), the real power consumption is inversely proportional to the square of the quality factor (\(P \propto \frac{1}{Q^2}\)).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not assume active power is independent of frequency. Even though \(P = I^2 R\), the current \(I\) depends heavily on the frequency-dependent inductive reactance \(X_L = \omega L\).

questions.subject: network-theory
questions.question: A water boiler at home is switched on the a.c. mains supplying power at 230V/ 50Hz. The frequency of instantaneous power consumed by the boiler is
questions.explanation: In the given problem, the supply is a single phase supply (household supply). We know that for a single phase system, the instantaneous power has double the frequency of the supply. \[p(t)=v(t)i(t)\] A boiler can be modelled as a resistance, hence \(i(t)=v(t)/R\) Thus \[p(t)=v(t)^2/R\] Given that \(v(t)=230\sqrt{2}\sin(2\pi.50t) V\) Thus, \[p(t)=\frac{230^2\times2}{R}sin^2(2\pi.50t)\] \[\text{or,}\frac{230^2\times2}{2R}(1-cos(2\times 2\pi.50t))\] \[\text{or,}\frac{230^2\times2}{2R}(1-cos( 2\pi.100t))\] Thus we can see that the frequency of instantaneous power (100Hz) is double that of the supply frequency (50 Hz). \[\boxed{(c)100Hz}\]

questions.subject: network-theory
questions.question:
The performance of a general two-port network \(N\) shown in the figure can be described in terms of its \(z\)-parameters or \(h\)-parameters as indicated below \[\begin{bmatrix} V_{1} \\ V_{2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} Z_{11} & Z_{12} \\ Z_{21} & Z_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} I_{1} \\ I_{2} \end{bmatrix}\] \[\begin{bmatrix} V_{1} \\ I_{2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} h_{11} & h_{12} \\ h_{21} & h_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} I_{1} \\ V_{2} \end{bmatrix}\] If the two-port is further characterized by additional constraints, a few conditions have to be satisfied by the parameters of the network. For each of the constraints specified in Table A, choose the appropriate condition to be satisfied, from amongst those listed in Table B.
Table ATable B
(a) Reciprocity at the ports(P) \(h_{11}h_{22} - h_{12}h_{21} = 1\)
(b) Passivity at the ports(Q) \(z_{12} = -z_{21}\)
(c) Electrical symmetry at the ports(R) \(h_{12} = h_{21}\)
(T) absence of negative resistors inside the 2-port
(U) energy input to the network from the ports is non-negative for all conditions at the ports
questions.explanation:
To determine the correct matching between the network properties in Table A and the conditions in Table B, let us analyze each constraint individually: 1. Reciprocity at the ports : A two-port network is reciprocal if the transmission of a signal from port 1 to port 2 is the same as from port 2 to port 1. In terms of open-circuit impedance parameters (\(z\)-parameters), the condition for reciprocity is defined as: \[z_{12} = z_{21}\] Looking at the choices provided in Table B, option (Q) shows \(z_{12} = -z_{21}\), which is the condition for an anti-reciprocal network, not a reciprocal one. Let us check the reciprocity condition in terms of hybrid parameters (\(h\)-parameters): \[h_{12} = -h_{21}\] Since this is also not listed, let's examine the provided solution context which indicates a typo in the original question's options or matching pairs, where (a) matches to an condition defining equal transfer impedances (\(z_{12} = z_{21}\)). Given the specific provided key where \(\text{(a)} \rightarrow \text{(Q)}\), it implies a direct matching based on the question text provided in the official key. 2. Passivity at the ports A passive network contains only energy-absorbing or energy-storing elements and cannot deliver net energy. For a passive network, there is an absence of negative resistance elements inside the two-port network because a negative resistance acts as an active element supplying power. Thus: \[\text{(b)} \rightarrow \text{(T)}\] 3. Electrical symmetry at the ports A two-port network is electrically symmetrical if its ports can be interchanged without changing the port voltages and currents. In terms of \(h\)-parameters, the condition for symmetry is that the determinant of the \(h\)-parameter matrix must be equal to unity: \[\Delta h = h_{11}h_{22} - h_{12}h_{21} = 1\] Thus: \[\text{(c)} \rightarrow \text{(P)}\]
Key points
  • Reciprocity Conditions: \(z_{12} = z_{21}\), \(y_{12} = y_{21}\), \(h_{12} = -h_{21}\), \(AD - BC = 1\).
  • Symmetry Conditions: \(z_{11} = z_{22}\), \(y_{11} = y_{22}\), \(h_{11}h_{22} - h_{12}h_{21} = 1\), \(A = D\).
  • Passivity: Requires that the total real power absorbed by the network is non-negative for all excitation conditions, implying no internal active elements or negative resistances.

questions.question: The depletion region or space charge region or transition in a semiconductor p-n junction diode has
questions.explanation: In a \(p\)-\(n\) junction, electrons and holes near the junction recombine after diffusion. As a result, the depletion region is left with only immobile ionized impurity atoms: \[\text{Donor atoms} \;\rightarrow\; \text{Positive ions} \ \qquad \ \text{Acceptor atoms} \;\rightarrow\; \text{Negative ions}\] Hence, the depletion region contains only positive and negative ions, with no free electrons or holes. Therefore, the correct answer is \[\boxed{\textbf{C. }\text{Positive ions and negative ions}}\]

questions.question: A non-inverting Op-Amp amplifier is shown in figure. The output voltage \(V_0\) is
questions.explanation:
Non-Inverting Terminal Voltage (\(V_+\)):
Using the superposition theorem and potential divider rule: \[V_+ = -2 \times \frac{R}{R + R} + (2 + \sin 100t) \times \frac{R}{R + R}\] \[V_+ = -1 + 1 + \frac{1}{2}\sin 100t = \frac{1}{2}\sin 100t\] Output Voltage (\(V_0\)):
For a non-inverting op-amp configuration with feedback resistance \(2R\) and input resistance \(R\): \[V_0 = \left(1 + \frac{2R}{R}\right) \times V_+ = 3 V_+\] \[V_0 = 3 \times \frac{1}{2}\sin 100t = \frac{3}{2}\sin 100t\] \[\boxed{(A) \ \ (3/2)\sin(100t)}\]

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: Let the magnitude of the gain in the inverting OP-Amp amplifier circuit shown in be \(x\) with switch \(S_1\) open. When the switch \(S_1\) is closed the magnitude of gain becomes
questions.explanation:
Case 1: Switch \(S_1\) Open
When switch \(S_1\) is open, the total feedback resistance \(R_{\text{f}}\) consists of two series resistors of value \(R\): \[R_{\text{f}} = R + R = 2R\] The magnitude of the voltage gain is: \[x = -\frac{2R}{R} = -2\] Case 2: Switch \(S_1\) Closed
When switch \(S_1\) is closed, one resistor \(R\) is short-circuited, making the effective feedback resistance \(R_{\text{f}}' = R\): The new gain \(x'\) is given by: \[x' = -\frac{R}{R} = -1\] Expressing \(x'\) in terms of \(x\): \[x' = \frac{x}{2}\] \[\boxed{\text{(A) x / 2}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The unit-impulse response of a unit-feedback control system is given by \[c(t) = -te^{-t} + 2e^{-t}, \quad (t \ge 0)\] the open loop transfer function is equal to
questions.explanation:
The closed-loop transfer function (\(\text{C.L.T.F.}\)) is the Laplace transform of the unit-impulse response: \[\text{C.L.T.F.} = \mathcal{L}\{c(t)\} = \mathcal{L}\{-te^{-t} + 2e^{-t}\} = \frac{-1}{(s + 1)^2} + \frac{2}{s + 1} = \frac{2s + 1}{(s + 1)^2}\] For a unity feedback system (\(H(s) = 1\)): \[\text{C.L.T.F.} = \frac{G(s)}{1 + G(s)} \implies G(s) = \frac{\text{C.L.T.F.}}{1 - \text{C.L.T.F.}}\] \[G(s) = \frac{\frac{2s + 1}{(s + 1)^2}}{1 - \frac{2s + 1}{(s + 1)^2}} = \frac{2s + 1}{(s^2 + 2s + 1) - (2s + 1)} = \frac{2s + 1}{s^2}\] \[\boxed{(B) \ \ \dfrac{2s + 1}{s^2}}\]
Key points
For unity feedback, the open-loop transfer function \(G(s)\) is related to the closed-loop transfer function \(T(s)\) by \(G(s) = \dfrac{T(s)}{1 - T(s)}\).

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: For a feedback control system of type 2, the steady state error for a ramp input is
questions.explanation: For a Type \(2\) system, the open-loop transfer function can be written as: \(G(s)H(s) = \dfrac{k}{s^2(s + a)}\) The steady-state error \(E_{ss}\) for a ramp input \(R(s) = \frac{1}{s^2}\) is given by: \[E_{ss} = \lim_{s \to 0} \frac{sR(s)}{1 + G(s)H(s)} = \lim_{s \to 0} \frac{s \left(\dfrac{1}{s^2}\right)}{1 + \dfrac{k}{s^2(s + a)}} = \lim_{s \to 0} \frac{1}{s + \dfrac{k}{s(s + a)}} = 0\] \[\boxed{\text{(C) zero}}\]

Statement for Linked Questions Q3.08.1 and Q3.08.2:
A \(240\,\text{V}\), dc shunt motor draws \(15\,\text{A}\) while supplying the rated load at a speed of \(80\,\text{rad/s}\). The armature resistance is \(0.5\,\Omega\) and the field winding resistance is \(80\,\Omega\).

Out of the following factors for a dc machine, (i) Interpole (ii) Armature resistance (iii) Armature leakage reactance (iv) Armature reaction (v) Reduction in field current The factors that are responsible for decrease in the terminal voltage of a shunt generator are
questions.explanation:
For a DC shunt generator, \[V_t = E_g - I_aR_a\] Thus, terminal voltage decreases either due to a reduction in generated EMF \(E_g\) or due to an increase in the internal voltage drop \(I_aR_a\). Examining each factor:
  • (i) Interpole: Interpoles improve commutation and do not directly affect terminal voltage.
  • (ii) Armature resistance: Causes a voltage drop \(I_aR_a\), thereby reducing terminal voltage.
  • (iii) Armature leakage reactance: Reactance is relevant in AC machines. In a DC generator, it does not contribute to steady-state terminal voltage reduction.
  • (iv) Armature reaction: Weakens the main field flux, reducing generated EMF.
  • (v) Reduction in field current: Since \[E_g \propto \phi \omega\] and \[\phi \propto I_f,\] a reduction in field current decreases flux and hence generated EMF.
Therefore, the factors responsible for a decrease in terminal voltage are \[(ii),\ (iv)\ \text{and}\ (v)\] Hence, \[\boxed{C}\]

Statement for Linked Questions (Q4.07.3,Q4.07.4 and Q4.07.5):
A three phase squirrel cage induction motor has a starting current of seven times the full load current and full load slip of \(5\%\).

Unbalanced supply voltage given to a \(3\)-phase, delta-connected induction motor will cause
questions.explanation:
An unbalanced three-phase supply can be resolved into symmetrical components as \[V = V_1 + V_2 + V_0\] where
  • \(V_1\) = positive-sequence component,
  • \(V_2\) = negative-sequence component,
  • \(V_0\) = zero-sequence component.
Any unbalanced set of three-phase voltages must contain positive- and negative-sequence components. The presence of a zero-sequence component depends on the availability of a return path and is not mandatory. In a three-phase induction motor, the negative-sequence component produces a backward rotating magnetic field, resulting in negative-sequence currents and additional heating. Therefore, an unbalanced supply voltage will cause Negative-sequence component current. Hence, the correct option is \[\boxed{C}\]

For an induction motor, the maximum torque is given by \[T_{\max} \propto V^2\] where \(V\) is the supply voltage. If the supply voltage is reduced by \(10\%\), \[V' = 0.9V\] Hence, \[\frac{T'_{\max}}{T_{\max}}
=
\left(\frac{V'}{V}\right)^2
=
(0.9)^2
=
0.81\] Therefore, \[T'_{\max}=0.81\,T_{\max}\] Percentage decrease in maximum torque: \[(1-0.81)\times 100
=
19\%\] Hence, the correct option is \[\boxed{C}\]

Statement for Linked Questions (Q4.07.3,Q4.07.4 and Q4.07.5):
A three phase squirrel cage induction motor has a starting current of seven times the full load current and full load slip of \(5\%\).

In an induction motor, if the air gap is increased
questions.explanation: The air-gap flux is given by \[\phi=\frac{\text{MMF}}{\mathcal{R}}\] where \(\mathcal{R}\) is the magnetic reluctance. If the air-gap length increases, the reluctance increases. To maintain the same flux, the magnetizing MMF must increase. Hence, the magnetizing current drawn from the supply increases. An increase in magnetizing current causes the input power factor of the induction motor to decrease. Therefore, statement (c) is correct. Further, an increase in air-gap length increases the leakage flux. Leakage flux is represented by the leakage reactance \(X_2\) of the induction motor. Since \[T_{\max}\propto \frac{1}{X_2}\] an increase in leakage reactance causes the maximum torque to decrease. Therefore, statement (d) is also correct. Hence, the correct options are \[\boxed{C,D}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question:
Statement for Linked Questions (Q5.05.2 and Q5.05.3):
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 83a & 83b: A \(1000\,\text{kVA}\), \(6.6\,\text{kV}\), \(3\)-phase star connected cylindrical pole synchronous generator has a synchronous reactance of \(20\,\Omega\). Neglect the armature resistance and consider operation at full load and unity power factor.

A cylindrical-rotor synchronous motor is connected to the supply with its field winding short-circuited. It will
options: start but not run at synchronous speed
start as an induction motor and then run as synchronous motor
start and run as a synchronous motor
questions.explanation: When the field winding of a cylindrical-rotor synchronous motor is short-circuited, no DC excitation is available. Hence, the motor cannot develop synchronous torque at standstill and therefore cannot start as a synchronous motor. However, the short-circuited field winding acts like a squirrel-cage rotor due to induced currents. Therefore, the machine develops induction motor torque and starts as an induction motor. As the field winding remains short-circuited, \[I_f = 0\] and no excitation emf is produced. \[E_f = 0\] Since synchronous torque is proportional to excitation, \[T_s \propto E_f\] \[T_s = 0\] Thus, after starting, the machine continues to operate only as an induction motor and cannot pull into synchronism. Hence, it starts but does not run at synchronous speed. \[\boxed{\text{B}}\]

In Figure, the characteristic that corresponds to the variation of synchronous reactance of a synchronous motor with field current is [figure unavailable]
questions.explanation:
The synchronous reactance of a synchronous motor is obtained from the ratio of open-circuit voltage to short-circuit current for the same field current. \[X_s=\frac{E_{oc}}{I_{sc}}\] At low values of field current, the magnetic circuit is unsaturated and \(X_s\) is nearly constant. As field current increases, saturation occurs, due to which the increase in \(E_{oc}\) is less than proportional. Therefore, \[I_f \uparrow \quad \Rightarrow \quad X_s \downarrow\] Hence, the curve corresponding to synchronous reactance versus field current is the decreasing curve. \[\boxed{\text{B}}\]
Key points
  • Synchronous reactance is given by \[X_s=\frac{E_{oc}}{I_{sc}}.\]
  • Due to saturation, synchronous reactance decreases with increase in field current.
  • The decreasing characteristic in the given figure is curve II.

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 83a & 83b: A \(1000\,\text{kVA}\), \(6.6\,\text{kV}\), \(3\)-phase star connected cylindrical pole synchronous generator has a synchronous reactance of \(20\,\Omega\). Neglect the armature resistance and consider operation at full load and unity power factor.

During hunting of synchronous motor
options: negative phase sequence currents are generated
harmonics are developed in the armature circuit
questions.explanation:
During hunting of a synchronous motor, the rotor oscillates about its equilibrium position. Due to these oscillations, relative motion exists between the rotor damper bars and the rotating magnetic field. Hence, currents are induced in the damper bars. These induced currents produce a damping torque which opposes the oscillations. Hence, the correct option is \[\boxed{\text{C}}\]
Key points
  • Hunting means oscillation of the rotor about synchronism.
  • Damper bars reduce hunting by producing damping torque.
  • The torque developed by damper bars opposes rotor oscillations.

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: In case of a split phase motor, the phase shift between currents in the two windings is around
questions.explanation:
In a split-phase induction motor, the main winding is highly inductive while the auxiliary winding is made more resistive. Because of the difference in the winding impedances, the currents in the two windings are displaced in phase. The phase difference obtained is approximately \[25^\circ \text{ to } 30^\circ\] Therefore, the correct option is \[\boxed{\text{A}}\]
Key points
  • Split-phase motors use resistance splitting to obtain starting torque.
  • Auxiliary winding current leads the main winding current.
  • Typical phase displacement is about \(25^\circ\)--\(30^\circ\).

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: The torque speed characteristic of a repulsion motor resembles which of the following dc motor characteristic?
questions.explanation:
A repulsion motor develops torque due to the interaction between stator flux and rotor currents induced through the commutator arrangement. The motor possesses
  • Very high starting torque
  • High starting current
  • Speed decreasing rapidly with load
These characteristics closely resemble those of a DC series motor. Therefore, the correct option is \[\boxed{\text{C}}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: Which type of motor is most suitable for computer printer drive?
questions.explanation:
Computer printers require precise angular positioning and accurate incremental motion. A stepper motor rotates through a fixed angle for every input pulse and provides excellent position control without requiring feedback. Therefore, stepper motors are widely used in
  • Computer printers
  • Plotters
  • CNC positioning systems
  • Robotics
Therefore, the correct option is \[\boxed{\text{D}}\]

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question: Which material is used in controlling chain reaction in a nuclear reactor?
questions.explanation:
Control rods regulate the neutron population inside a nuclear reactor. The material used for control rods should have a high neutron-absorption cross section. Boron satisfies this requirement and effectively absorbs excess neutrons. Therefore the fission chain reaction can be controlled by inserting or withdrawing boron control rods. \[\boxed{\text{(C)}\;\text{Boron}}\]
Key points
  • Boron and cadmium are common control-rod materials.
  • Heavy water acts mainly as a moderator.
  • Thorium is a fertile fuel material.

Answer the questions Q\(2.05.1\) and Q\(2.05.2\) based on the data below: At a 220 kV substation of a power system, it is given that the three-phase fault level is 4000 MVA and the single-line-to-ground fault level is 5000 MVA. Neglecting the resistance and the shunt susceptances of the system.

For an unbalanced fault, with paths for zero-sequence currents, at the point of fault
options: the negative and zero sequence voltages are minimum
the negative and zero sequence voltages are maximum
the negative sequence voltage is minimum and zero sequence voltage is maximum
the negative sequence voltage is maximum and zero sequence voltage is minimum
questions.explanation:
An unbalanced fault causes negative-sequence currents and voltages to appear. If the fault path permits zero-sequence current flow (such as ground faults), zero-sequence components also become significant. At the fault point:
  • Negative-sequence effects are strongest.
  • Zero-sequence effects are strongest.
  • Hence the corresponding sequence voltages attain their maximum values relative to other system locations.
Therefore, \[\boxed{\text{(B)}\; \text{Negative- and zero-sequence voltages are maximum}}\]

questions.question:
Answer the questions Q\(3.06.1\) and Q\(3.06.2\) based on the data below A generator feeds power to an infinite bus through a double circuit transmission line. A Three-phase fault occurs at the middle point of one of the lines. The infinite bus voltage is \(1\) pu, the transient internal voltage of the generator is \(1.1\) pu and the equivalent transfer admittance during fault is \(0.8\) pu. The \(100\) MVA generator has an inertia constant of \(5\) MJ/MVA and was delivering \(1.0\) pu power prior to the fault with rotor power angle of \(30^\circ\). The system frequency is \(50\) Hz.

During a disturbance on a synchronous machine, the rotor swings from A to B, before finally settling down to a steady state at point C on the power-angle curve. The speed of the machine during oscillation is synchronous at point(s)
questions.explanation:
During rotor oscillations, the machine alternately accelerates and decelerates about the equilibrium position. At the extreme points of the swing:
  • Rotor speed becomes equal to synchronous speed.
  • Relative speed deviation becomes zero.
  • Direction of rotor acceleration changes.
These extreme points correspond to A and B. Point C is the final steady-state operating point reached after damping has removed oscillations. Hence, the required option is \[\boxed{\text{(A)}\;\text{A and B}}\]

options: the system losses will be unchanged but complex bus voltages will change
the system losses will change but complex bus voltages remain unchanged
the system losses as well as complex bus voltage will change
the system losses as well as complex bus voltage will be unchanged
questions.explanation:
The slack bus is introduced only to balance real and reactive power mismatches. Changing the reference bus does not alter:
  • Transmission-line parameters.
  • Load data.
  • Generator schedules.
Hence the physical system losses remain unchanged. However, bus-voltage phasors are measured relative to the selected reference bus angle. Changing the reference bus changes the numerical representation of the complex bus voltages. Therefore, \[\boxed{\text{(A)}\; \text{the system losses will be unchanged but complex bus voltages will change}}\]

questions.explanation: Resistance switching is used to reduce transient overvoltages during current interruption. Air-blast circuit breakers interrupt current very rapidly and can generate severe switching surges. A resistor is temporarily inserted during switching to damp these transients. The SCR is rated at \(1.5\,\text{kV}\), \(250\,\text{A}\) with \(I_L=250\,\text{mA}\), \(I_H=150\,\text{mA}\), \(I_{G\max}=150\,\text{mA}\), and \(I_{G\min}=100\,\text{mA}\). The SCR is connected to an inductive load, where \(L=150\,\text{mH}\) in series with a small resistance and the supply voltage is \(200\,\text{V dc}\). The forward drops of all transistors/diodes and the gate-cathode junction during ON state are \(1.0\,\text{V}\). [figure unavailable]

Which semiconductor power device out of the following is not a current triggered device?
questions.explanation:
Power semiconductor devices are classified based on their control mechanisms.
  • SCR (Thyristor): Current-triggered device. A gate current initiates conduction.
  • GTO (Gate Turn-Off Thyristor): Current-controlled device. Positive gate current turns it ON, and negative gate current turns it OFF.
  • TRIAC: Current-triggered bidirectional thyristor. A gate current triggers conduction in either direction.
  • MOSFET: Voltage-controlled device. It is turned ON/OFF by the gate-to-source voltage with negligible steady-state gate current.
Hence, the only device that is not current triggered is the MOSFET. \[\boxed{D}\]

The SCR is connected to an inductive load, where \(L=150\,\text{mH}\) in series with a small resistance and the supply voltage is \(200\,\text{V dc}\). The Triac can be used only in
questions.explanation:
A TRIAC is a bidirectional thyristor capable of conducting current in both directions. Hence, it is suitable only for AC power control applications. Among the given options:
  • Inverter uses forced commutation devices such as MOSFETs or IGBTs.
  • Rectifiers generally employ SCRs or diodes.
  • Multiquadrant choppers require self-commutating devices.
  • Cycloconverters use TRIACs (or anti-parallel SCRs) for direct AC-to-AC conversion.
Therefore, the TRIAC can be used only in a cycloconverter. \[\boxed{D}\]

Which of the following does not cause permanent damage to an SCR?
options: High rate of rise of current
High rate of rise of voltage
questions.explanation:
A high rate of rise of voltage can cause false triggering due to \(dv/dt\) triggering, but it cannot cause permanent damage to an SCR. The other three factors can cause thermal damage to the SCR. \[\boxed{D}\]
Key points
  • Excessive \(dv/dt\) may turn ON an SCR unintentionally due to junction capacitance.
  • Excessive \(di/dt\) causes localized heating near the gate region.
  • Overcurrent and excessive junction temperature can permanently damage the SCR.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not confuse false triggering due to \(dv/dt\) with permanent device failure.
  • Remember that \(dv/dt\) protection is provided using an RC snubber circuit.
  • Thermal damage is mainly associated with excessive current or temperature, not with \(dv/dt\) alone.

In a thyristor dc chopper, which type of commutation results in best performance?
questions.explanation:
Voltage commutation provides the best performance in a DC chopper. It offers advantages such as:
  • Higher average output voltage.
  • Faster and more reliable turn-off of the thyristor.
  • Better overall efficiency and performance.
Hence, the correct answer is \[\boxed{{(A) \ \text{Voltage commutation}}}\]

questions.question: The moving coil in a dynamometer wattmeter is connected
options: in series with the fixed coil
questions.explanation:
[figure unavailable] A dynamometer wattmeter has:
  • Fixed coil (Current coil, CC) Connected in series with the load, hence: \[I_{CC}=I_{\text{load}}\]
  • Moving coil (Pressure/Potential coil, PC) Connected across the supply through a high resistance, hence: \[I_{PC}\propto V\]
The interaction of: \[\text{Magnetic field due to CC}\propto I\] and \[\text{Current in PC}\propto V\] produces deflecting torque: \[T_d\propto VI\cos\phi\] Thus the wattmeter measures power. Why other options are wrong: A. In series with fixed coil \(\times\) Then the moving coil would carry load current instead of voltage-proportional current. C. In series with load \(\times\) This is the connection of the current coil. D. Across the load
Practically load and supply voltages are nearly same, but standard wattmeter terminology states: \[\boxed{ \text{Pressure coil is connected across the supply} }\] The correct answer is: \[\boxed{ \textbf{B. } \text{ across the supply} }\]
